newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 22.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 22. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said Indonesia's capital market law did not restrict share ownership in companies listed on local exchanges after President Suharto suggested single share ownership in listed firms should be limited to 15 percent. Mar'ie said the law only imposed a 49 percent limit on foreign ownership.

Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto said small air cargo jets that carry perishable goods will not be restricted to Batam island near Singapore but will also be able to fly into Manado in North Sulawesi and Ujung Padang in South Sulawesi.

Twenty foreign journalists who had hoped to go to the East Timor capital of Dili to cover the blessing on Sunday of a 27-foot high statue of Jesus Christ by Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo have had their travel permits withdrawn hours after they had been issued.

Police have given to state prosecutors the results of their investigation into the murder of a Yogyakarta journalist. Journalist and human rights groups have said they doubt that the man accused by the police is actual killer.
